question:
A 41-year-old man is being evaluated after an elevated serum creatinine level was identified during a
routine check-up. He has no acute complaints but recalls being told years ago that he had cysts in both
kidneys. His family history includes polycystic kidney disease in his father and paternal uncle, with his
father undergoing dialysis three times per week. There is no family history of intracranial bleeding,
stroke, or sudden unexplained death. On examination, his blood pressure is 158/73 mm Hg, heart rate
is 83 beats per minute, temperature is 37■C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on ambient air. Both
kidneys are palpable, and the rest of the physical examination is unremarkable. Laboratory findings
reveal a serum creatinine level of 1.5 mg/dL (reference range, 0.8–1.3), with a normal basic metabolic
panel, urinalysis, and urine protein-to-creatinine ratio. Which of the following diagnostic tests is most
appropriate at this time to assess for extrarenal manifestations of the suspected condition? Answer
Choices: (A) Serum aldosterone-to-renin ratio to evaluate for secondary hypertension (B) MRI of the
spine to evaluate for spinal cord compression (C) Abdominal CT with contrast to evaluate for liver cysts
(D) Complete ultrasound of the abdomen (E) CT of the head (F) Genetic testing to confirm the
diagnosis (G) Echocardiography to assess for valvular abnormalities (H) Magnetic resonance
venography of the head and neck (I) Bone densitometry to assess for osteoporosis (J) Renal biopsy to
assess for glomerular damage
 A. Genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
B. Echocardiography to assess for valvular abnormalities
C. Abdominal CT with contrast to evaluate for liver cysts
D. Magnetic resonance venography of the head and neck
E. MRI of the spine to evaluate for spinal cord compression
F. Serum aldosterone-to-renin ratio to evaluate for secondary hypertension
G. Bone densitometry to assess for osteoporosis
H. Renal biopsy to assess for glomerular damage
I. CT of the head
J. Complete ultrasound of the abdomen
